info.text: Unit 6 — Toolbox talk and the Dirty Dozen. Listening, Reading, Use of English, Vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listening — Dialogue 1. Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What was the main human factor behind the near-miss?

generalfeedback.text: The team lead says a phone call took the technician's attention off the job, so distraction was the main factor. Complacency added to it, but it was not the main one.

feedback.text: Correct — the call pulled his attention off the flap inspection.

answer.text: A worn or faulty control cable

feedback.text: No — it was a human factor, not a technical fault.

answer.text: A wrong torque on the flap bolts

feedback.text: No — torque is not mentioned in Dialogue 1.

answer.text: Poor lighting near the flap track

feedback.text: No — lighting is not the factor named in the dialogue.

questiontext.text: Listening — Dialogue 1. Listen again. The speakers agree that complacency also played a part, because the task felt routine.

generalfeedback.text: Elena adds complacency, and the team lead agrees: "He had done that task many times, so he felt over-confident." So the statement is true.

feedback.text: Correct — routine work quietly lowered his awareness.
Listen again — both speakers name complacency as a second factor.

questiontext.text: Listening — Dialogue 2. Listen to Dialogue 2 again. Which unsafe norm does Elena raise?

generalfeedback.text: Elena says the team "sometimes sign the checklist first, and then finish the task afterwards." Signing before the work is done is the unsafe norm.

answer.text: Signing the checklist before the task is done

feedback.text: Correct — the checklist only defends you if each step is ticked honestly.

answer.text: Leaving loose hand tools uncounted on the hangar floor

feedback.text: No — this norm is not the one Elena raises.
No — the talk is happening; that is not the norm.

answer.text: Working alone on a night shift

feedback.text: No — working alone is not the norm she names.

questiontext.text: Listening — Dialogue 3. Listen again. The rule agreed is that you must not take a call while your hands are inside the aircraft.

generalfeedback.text: The team lead says: "You must not take a call while your hands are inside the aircraft." The statement matches the audio, so it is true.

feedback.text: Correct — phones off near an open panel; no calls with hands inside.
Listen again — this is stated as a firm rule with "must not".

questiontext.text: Listening — Dialogue 4 (PA announcement). Listen again. How many minutes long is the safety stand-down? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: The announcement says "a two-minute safety stand-down", so the answer is 2.

feedback.text: Correct — a two-minute stand-down.

questiontext.text: Listening — Dialogue 1. Listen again. How many items are there in the Dirty Dozen? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: The team lead says distraction is "one of the twelve items in the Dirty Dozen", so the answer is 12.

feedback.text: Correct — twelve human factors.

questiontext.text:
Reading — task card.

TASK CARD 32-11-05 — Nose landing gear, daily check.
Step 4: Torque the two access-panel bolts to 8 Nm.
Step 5: Fit lockwire to both bolts.
Step 6: A second technician must cross-check steps 4 and 5 and sign block 6B.

What must a second technician do?

generalfeedback.text: Step 6 requires an independent cross-check of the torque (step 4) and the lockwire (step 5), with a signature in block 6B.

answer.text: Cross-check steps 4 and 5 and sign block 6B

feedback.text: Correct — an independent cross-check of the torque and the lockwire.

answer.text: Re-torque both access-panel bolts to eight newton-metres

feedback.text: No — the first technician sets the torque; the second checks it.

answer.text: Remove the lockwire and refit new wire

feedback.text: No — the card asks for a check, not a refit.

answer.text: Defer the task to the next daily check

feedback.text: No — nothing on the card allows deferral.

questiontext.text:
Reading — tech log entry.

TECH LOG — YL-BBC.
Defect: right landing light inoperative.
Crew ref MEL 33-40-01a: item may be deferred for 10 days.
Action: light isolated and placarded; deferred per MEL.
Cross-checked by B2 engineer.

Statement: The defect was fully repaired before the next flight.

generalfeedback.text: The entry says the item was "deferred per MEL" — isolated and placarded, not repaired. So the statement is false.

feedback.text: Correct — under the MEL the defect was deferred, not repaired.
Re-read — the action was to isolate, placard and defer, not to repair.

questiontext.text:
Reading — service bulletin.

SERVICE BULLETIN SB A320-27-1189.
Reason: reports of chafing on a flap-control cable near an access panel.
Compliance: recommended within 600 flight hours.
Action: inspect the cable run; if chafing is found, replace the cable.

When is compliance recommended?

generalfeedback.text: The compliance line states "recommended within 600 flight hours." The action is to inspect, and replace only if chafing is found.

feedback.text: Correct — the recommended compliance window.
No — check the figure again; it is 600.
No — the bulletin gives a flight-hours window.
No — inspection is recommended within the window, not only after a report.

questiontext.text:
Reading — work order.

WORK ORDER WO-5521.
Task: replace cabin oxygen bottle.
Note: safety-critical task — hold a toolbox talk before start and a debrief after.
Sign-off requires an independent cross-check.

Statement: Sign-off of this task needs an independent cross-check.

generalfeedback.text: The work order states sign-off "requires an independent cross-check", so the statement is true.

feedback.text: Correct — a safety-critical task needs an independent cross-check.
Re-read — the sign-off line requires a cross-check.

questiontext.text:
Use of English. Complete the rule. Write ONE word in the gap.

You must ______ take a call near an open panel. (prohibition)

generalfeedback.text: Prohibition is must not + base verb. The missing word after "must" is not.

feedback.text: Correct — "must not" marks a firm prohibition.

questiontext.text:
Use of English. Correct the verb. Write ONE word.

He should checks ______ the lockwire twice.

generalfeedback.text: A modal takes the base verb with no third-person "-s". "should checks" becomes should check.

feedback.text: Correct — base verb after a modal, no "-s".

questiontext.text:
Use of English. Write ONE word in the gap.

We ______ to double-check every torque. (advice — the modal that keeps "to")

generalfeedback.text: "ought to" is the one modal that keeps its "to". The missing word is ought.

feedback.text: Correct — "ought to double-check".

questiontext.text:
Use of English. Correct the error. Rewrite the modal phrase (two words).

Wrong: "We must to check the torque." → Right: "We ______ ______ the torque."

generalfeedback.text: Drop the "to" after "must": must check. A modal is followed by the base verb.

feedback.text: Correct — no "to" after "must".

questiontext.text:
Use of English — bank term. Write the term (one hyphenated word).

A check of your work by a second person is a ______.

generalfeedback.text: A second person checking your work is a cross-check (you checking again yourself is a double-check).

feedback.text: Correct — a second-person check.
Accepted — the usual spelling is "cross-check".

questiontext.text:
Use of English — bank term. Write the term (one word).

Over-confidence that grows from routine work, so you stop checking, is ______.

generalfeedback.text: Over-confidence from routine is complacency — a Dirty Dozen factor.

feedback.text: Correct — routine lowers your guard.

questiontext.text:
Use of English — transformation. Rewrite with a modal of NO obligation. Write the missing modal phrase (three words).

"It is not necessary to blame anyone." → "We ______ ______ ______ blame anyone."

generalfeedback.text: "Not necessary" = no obligation: do not have to (or "don't have to"). "need not" also works but is two words.

feedback.text: Correct — "do not have to blame anyone".
Accepted — "don't have to blame anyone".
Accepted — full form of the phrase.

questiontext.text: Vocabulary. Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: near-miss = almost harm; fatigue = tiredness; norms = accepted habits; debrief = review after a job; assertiveness = speaking up.

answer.text: an event that almost caused harm
being very tired, so you make mistakes
unsafe habits a team quietly accepts
a short review talk after a job
speaking up firmly about a safety concern
a written record of an unsafe event

questiontext.text: Vocabulary — collocations. Match each word to the word it goes with.

generalfeedback.text: Common partners: time + pressure; situational + awareness; incident + report; torque + setting; break + the error chain.

questiontext.text: Vocabulary. Which word means "speaking up firmly about a safety concern"?

generalfeedback.text: Speaking up firmly, even when it feels awkward, is assertiveness — a Dirty Dozen factor when it is missing.

feedback.text: Correct — raising a worry firmly and early.
No — that is over-confidence from routine.
No — that is attention leaving the task.
No — that is not knowing what is going on around you.

questiontext.text: Vocabulary. Which part is "thin wire that stops a bolt turning loose"?

generalfeedback.text: Lockwire ties fasteners so vibration cannot back them off. Torque is the tightness; a checklist is a list of steps.

feedback.text: Correct — it physically locks a bolt against vibration.
No — that is a list of steps you tick off.
No — that is the tightness set on the bolt.
No — that is a written record of an unsafe event.
